title: An invariant geometric germ has a section over its finite separable field
statement: Let $K\subset K_s\subset\Omega$ be a compatible field tower [def-pc-field-extension], with $K_s$ a separable closure of $K$ [def-kun-separably-closed] and $\Omega$ algebraically closed and algebraic over $K$. Let $s=\operatorname{Spec}(K\to\Omega)$ be the geometric point [def-weil-geometric-point], and let $F$ be a sheaf of sets on $(\operatorname{Spec}K)_{\mathrm{et}}$ [def-weil-pbc-etale-site], with geometric stalk $M$ [def-weil-pbc-geometric-stalks]. Suppose a left action $a$ of $G=\operatorname{Gal}(K_s/K)$ on $M$ satisfies $a(g,[X,x,z])=[X,\operatorname{Spec}(\tau)\mathbin{;}x,z]$ whenever $\tau\in\operatorname{Aut}_K(\Omega)$ extends $g$. Let $L\subset K_s$ be a finite separable intermediate extension, and let $x:\operatorname{Spec}\Omega\to\operatorname{Spec}L$ be the specified lift induced by $L\hookrightarrow K_s\hookrightarrow\Omega$. For every $m\in M$ fixed by $H_L=\operatorname{Gal}(K_s/L)$, there exists $z\in F(\operatorname{Spec}L)$ with germ $[\operatorname{Spec}L,x,z]=m$.

source.place: Tags 03QW and 04JM; read at https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/03QW and https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/04JM

proof.text: Restrict the sheaf from Spec K to Spec L by etale composition. Pointed neighbourhoods over Spec L form a cofinal system among those over Spec K, by taking their fibre product with Spec L and using the chosen lift x. Thus this restriction computes the same geometric stalk.

source.place: Tags 03QW and 04JM; read at https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/03QW and https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/04JM

proof.text: Represent m by a section in a pointed etale neighbourhood. Shrink to the singleton component containing the lift; the etale fibre theorem identifies it with the spectrum of a finite separable extension. The chosen lift embeds its residue field in Omega, and separability places its image in Ks. Take the images of finite K-bases of this field and L in Ks. FiniteGaloisIntermediateField.adjoin K of their union constructs a finite Galois subfield E of Ks containing both images. It is also Galois over L. Its inclusions preserve the already specified lifts. Pull back the representative to Spec E.

source.place: Tags 03QW and 04JM; read at https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/03QW and https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/04JM

proof.text: The germ map over Spec E is injective: cofilteredness gives a common pointed refinement witnessing equality of germs; the refinement maps surjectively to the one-point Spec E because its lift makes it nonempty. Its map is etale, hence a cover. Separatedness makes its restriction map injective.

source.place: Tags 03QW and 04JM; read at https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/03QW and https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/04JM

proof.text: Every L-automorphism of the finite Galois field E extends to an L-automorphism of Ks (normal algebraic extension), and thence to an automorphism of Omega. The supplied lift-change formula and invariance of m identify the germs of the representative and its automorphism pullback. Germ injectivity gives equality of those sections.

source.place: Tags 03QW and 04JM; read at https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/03QW and https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/04JM

proof.text: Apply finite Galois sections descent to the restricted sheaf to obtain a section over Spec L with that representative as pullback. Naturality of the colimit injections shows its germ at the specified x is m.
